# Forming a country needs a primary culture from its definition's list, and vanilla's lists name the parts of the
# culture merges. A part that has switched leaves a country's primary cultures (te_cm_monthly_switched_culture), so
# each list gains the merged cultures its parts become (owner, 2026-11-09): a Germany that is only German can still
# form the Holy Roman Empire. Only tags that own no state at the 1836 start, so no country begins with a merged
# culture that has no people; a start tag (RUS, PRU, GBR) holds its parts while it is dead instead
# (te_cmg_part_held_<c>). Each block restates vanilla's whole list (from culture_merge_primary_reads.json), so the
# result is right whether the engine appends an injected list to vanilla's or puts it in its place; the self-check
# cm_definition_inject reads one tag. Forming adds every listed culture, so te_cmg_strip_untouched_results takes a
# merged culture whose merge never began off again.
